item.title: 75-YO Varanasi Artist Turns Wedding Cards & Broken Bangles Into Stunning Art
item.description: In Varanasi, where the Ganga River murmurs age‑old prayers and pilgrims circle life’s biggest rites, an unlikely artist is weaving magic from the city’s overlooked remains. At 75, Rajkumar walks the ghats with a practised eye, gathering what most would dismiss as refuse, discarded wedding cards, broken bangles, frayed paper, and stray scraps of metal and cloth. To the casual observer, these are remnants of rituals, celebrations and daily life, detritus left in the wake of devotees and tourists.

item.title: Step Into Goa’s Hidden Carnival: Rare Glimpses of Shigmotsav Celebrations
item.description: “Rice is cooked on people’s heads.” This is Varun Hegde’s favourite story to tell about the Shisharanni ritual as he escorts travellers into Goa’s villages every March, where the locals prepare to celebrate Shigmo — the harvest festival that heralds spring. Varun pauses to allow the dramatic gasp that always follows his tale.
